action: Organisations using Maileva: ask which of your recipients are affected and whether you must notify them or the regulator. People in France: be wary of letters, calls or messages that use your name and address to seem genuine.
exec: A breach at a mailing supplier exposed data that client organisations, including healthcare and housing bodies, had entrusted to it.
plain: A cyberattack on Maileva, a mail-services company owned by France's La Poste, exposed the names and postal addresses of about 22 million people whose letters it handles for other organisations.
summary: A cyberattack on Maileva, La Poste's mail-services subsidiary, exposed names and postal addresses of about 22 million people. They include patients and tenants whose letters it handles for client organizations.
title: Breach at La Poste subsidiary Maileva exposes 22 million people in France
